title: Relative reductive groups, multiplicative type, centres and maximal-torus quotient squares
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use group objects in schemes over $S$ as in [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. Use scheme base change [def-pc-base-change], closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion], smoothness [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A relative group $C$ is of multiplicative type if there is an fppf covering by affine schemes $\operatorname{Spec}R_i\to S$ such that $C_{R_i}$ is isomorphic as a group scheme to $D_{R_i}(N_i)$, with $N_i$ a finitely generated abelian group [def-sfb-ring-diagonalizable-group]. A relative group $G$ is reductive if its structure map is smooth, affine and finite type, and every pullback to an algebraically closed field is reductive in the sense of [def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology]. A homomorphism $i:T\to G$ is a relative maximal torus if it is a closed immersion, $T$ is a relative torus [def-sfb-relative-torus], and its pullback to every algebraically closed field is a maximal torus in the sense of [def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology]. A homomorphism $c:C\to G$ is central if $c(a)$ commutes with every $g\in G(U)$ for every $S$-scheme $U$ and $a\in C(U)$. A homomorphism $z:Z\to G$ represents the centre if it is a closed immersion and, on every $S$-scheme $U$, its image is exactly the set of $g\in G(U)$ whose restriction to every $V\to U$ commutes with every point in $G(V)$. For homomorphisms $c:C\to G$ and $p:G\to Q$, a maximal-torus quotient square consists of homomorphisms $i:T\to G$, $j:U\to Q$, $q:T\to U$, with $i,j$ relative maximal tori, the square $(i,q,p,j)$ cartesian, and a factorization $k:C\to T$ satisfying $i\circ k=c$ such that $(k,q)$ presents the fppf quotient $T/C=U$ [def-sfb-fppf-group-quotient-presentation]. Say $c,p$ have the maximal-torus correspondence if every maximal torus inclusion in $G$ occurs as $i$ in such a square, every maximal torus inclusion in $Q$ occurs as $j$, and the pullback of every such square along every morphism $S'\to S$ is again such a square. The cartesian condition makes the two projections of this relation inverse on subgroup schemes, so this describes a bijection of maximal torus subgroups rather than a choice of their presentations. No nonempty-base, globally constant-rank, characteristic or smoothness-of-$C$ hypothesis is part of these definitions.
